1. Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp spikes — reduce initial forecast values by 5–10% relative to historical mean or recent peak.

2. Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon — adjust downward by 2–5% to align with observed mean reversion toward prior 30-day average.

3. Forecast tends to overshoot after a price spike (e.g., 60→70→75), then corrects — apply a “cool-down” rule: if forecast > 1.2x recent high, reduce by 10–15% for next 3–5 days.

4. Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices in the first 10 days — apply a “lag correction”: subtract 2–4% from first 10 forecast days if historical mean is below 65.

5. Forecast mean is often 5–8% above true outcome — apply a global downward bias correction: subtract 3–5% from all forecast values if mean of 30-day history is > 60.

6. Model fails to capture mean reversion in 3–5 day windows — apply a “reversion filter”: if forecast deviates > 3σ from 30-day moving average, adjust toward MA with 50% weight on recent 7-day average.
